summary: Higher-order contract wrapping implementation is correct for core use cases. Blame assignment logic verified correct.

blame_assignment.note: Domain violations blame caller, range violations blame callee - verified correct

blame_flip.note: Blame correctly flips when crossing HO boundaries - if callback is broken, caller blamed; if callback misused, callee blamed

arity_checking.note: wrap-function explicitly checks argument count against domain contract length

recursive_wrapping.note: Nested HO functions wrapped recursively with proper blame propagation

listof_vectorof.note: Container combinators (listof, vectorof) are flat contracts - cannot contain function contracts
listof_vectorof.impact: (listof (->c ...)) will fail - function contracts in containers not supported
listof_vectorof.recommendation: Future: implement chaperone-style wrappers for HO contracts in data structures

boolean_combinators.note: and/c, or/c, not/c are flat contract operations - cannot combine function contracts
boolean_combinators.recommendation: Future: extend combinators to produce wrapped functions for HO cases

dependent_contracts.note: Dep contract wrapping explicitly returns error - documented as future work

implemented: check-and-wrap-args - domain checking with HO wrapping
apply-contract - convenience wrapper that raises on violation

conclusion: The higher-order contract wrapping implementation correctly handles the core use case of function contracts with proper blame assignment. Known limitations (flat-only combinators, no dependent contracts) are documented and acceptable for current scope. The blame flip logic for nested HO functions has been verified correct through static analysis.
